claims.text: The as-built Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA is an additively manufactured dual-nanoprecipitation alloy.
High-temperature oxidation causes selective elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitates in this HEA.
Nanoprecipitates act as active sites for elemental redistribution during oxidation.
The redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates leads to formation of protective oxide layers.
The resulting protective oxide layers enhance the alloy's oxidation resistance.
Nanoprecipitates are dispersed throughout the alloy matrix.
Nanoprecipitate interfaces may concentrate selected elements and thereby influence oxide nucleation and growth.
APT provides near-atomic-resolution three-dimensional compositional mapping.
APT can detect redistribution of Ti, Al, Cr, and other constituents during oxidation.
Enrichment of oxidation-resistant elements at nanoprecipitates could promote a continuous, adherent oxide scale.
A continuous, adherent oxide scale limits further oxidation.
Conventional XRD and SEM oxidation studies cannot resolve the fine-scale elemental segregation proposed to mediate oxidation behavior.
Complex multiphase microstructures and APT specimen-preparation artifacts may limit interpretation.
TEM-EDS mapping may be required to validate APT-derived segregation patterns.
Preferential evaporation can reduce the quantitative accuracy of APT measurements in complex multicomponent systems.
Absence of detectable oxidation-induced enrichment or oxygen segregation at nanoprecipitates would falsify the proposed nanoprecipitate-mediated mechanism.
